Term1: Reactivation of primary infection (zoster or shingles)
Text:
# REACTIVATION OF PRIMARY INFECTION (ZOSTER OR SHINGLES)

Zoster represents reactivation of varicella-zoster virus. After primary infection, virus remains latent in the sensory dorsal root ganglia. Reactivation syndrome is characterized by painful, unilateral, vesicular,
dermatomal rash.

## Prevention

Vaccinate all adults greater than or equal to 50 years of age with the recombinant zoster vaccine regardless of past episode or receipt of the live zoster vaccine.

Give recombinant zoster vaccine x2, 2nd dose 2-6 months after the first.

## ________________________________

References:

Therapy:
## Immunocompetent patients

## Treatment in persons <50 years

Treatment is not beneficial, none is recommended.

## Treatment in persons >=50 years

Treatment with antivirals can shorten duration of pain and rash in patients over 50 years old. Treatment must be started within 72 hours of onset.

Valacyclovir 1000 mg PO q8h for 7 days ($) [R]

There is evidence that addition of corticosteroids to antiviral therapy decreases pain and duration of rash and improves quality of life modestly during the acute shingles episode. Corticosteroids do not decrease the incidence of post-herpetic neuralgia. Some authorities recommend addition of
corticosteroid therapy to antiviral therapy for patients over age 50 years.

Corticosteroids are not recommended for patients at greater risk for steroid toxicities (e.g., insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, hypertension, peptic ulcer disease) or for immunocompromised patients.

Optional Recommendation:
Prednisone 60 mg daily for 7 days then 30 mg daily for 7 days, then 15 mg daily for 7 days. ($)

## Outpatient Guidance

## Treatment in persons >=50 years

Valacyclovir 1000 mg PO TID for 7 days ($) [R]

## Immunocompromised patients

## Treatment

Immunocompromised patients at increased risk for complications of VZV disease include: patients with malignancy, current immunosuppressive therapy, or HIV infection. Treatment with antivirals shortens duration of symptoms and reduces incidence of complications. In immunocompromised patients, treatment is recommended to be started at any point during an active infection.

## Treatment for mild to moderate disease

Valacyclovir 1000 mg PO q8h for 7 days ($) [R]

## Treatment for severe disease or progression from mild to moderate disease in patients <=65 years

Acyclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h for 7-14 days ($$) [R]

## Treatment for severe disease or progression from mild to moderate disease in patients >65 years

Acyclovir 7.5 mg/kg IV q8h for 7-14 days($$) [R]
